operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of timesheets.

This operation provides search capabilities for timesheets within the current organization context. Employees can only view their own timesheets, while users with time:approve permission can view all employees' timesheets for approval workflow management.

Supports filtering by timesheet status (draft, submitted, approved, rejected) and date range (week_start_date boundaries). The response includes timesheet summaries optimized for list displays with key information such as status, total hours, and submission dates.

When an employee views their timesheets, the results are automatically scoped to that employee. When a user with time:approve permission views timesheets, results include all employees' timesheets within the organization.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query erp_hrm_timesheets table with organization-scoped filtering.

1. Extract organization context from the authenticated session.
2. If the current user has time:approve permission:
   - Apply optional status filter (draft, submitted, approved, rejected)
   - Apply optional employee_id filter to scope results to specific employee
   - Apply optional week_start_date range filters (gte/lte for date boundaries)
3. If the current user does NOT have time:approve permission:
   - Automatically scope results to the current user's employee record
   - Apply same optional filters as above (except employee_id, which is fixed)
4. Apply pagination with configurable page size (default 20, max 100) and cursor-based pagination using created_at for consistent ordering.
5. Join with erp_hrm_employees table to include employee name in summary (for approvers viewing all employees' timesheets).
6. Order by created_at descending (newest first).
7. Calculate total_hours from the timesheet's included timelogs.
8. Return paginated results with IPageIErpHrmTimesheet.ISummary format.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of timesheet summaries matching the search criteria

requestBody.description: Search criteria including optional filters for status, date range, employee, and pagination parameters

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific timesheet by its unique identifier.

This endpoint returns detailed information about a single timesheet including its status, date range, total hours, included timelogs, and review information. The response includes the owning employee details and reviewer information when the timesheet has been reviewed.

The owning employee can view their own timesheets in any status. Users with time:view_all permission can view all employees' timesheets. Users with time:approve permission can view submitted, approved, or rejected timesheets for approval workflow purposes.

When the timesheet status is rejected, the response includes the rejection_reason field populated by the reviewing user. Approved timesheets have all their included timelogs locked from editing.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query erp_hrm_timesheets table by id (UUID primary key).

Join with erp_hrm_employees to include employee details (id, position, employment_type, status).

Join with erp_hrm_employees (reviewer) when reviewer_employee_id is not null to include reviewer details.

Join with erp_hrm_timesheet_timelogs and erp_hrm_timelogs to include all associated timelog entries.

For each included timelog, include: id, date, duration_minutes, description, billable, project_id, task_id, created_at.

Authorization:
- If requester is the owning employee: allow access to their own timesheet
- If requester has time:view_all permission: allow access to any timesheet in the organization
- If requester has time:approve permission: allow access to timesheets in submitted/approved/rejected status
- Otherwise: return 403 Forbidden

Return 404 Not Found if timesheet does not exist or belongs to a different organization.

Soft-deleted timesheets (deleted_at is not null) should return 404.

responseBody.description: The complete timesheet entity with included timelogs, employee, and reviewer information.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timesheet to retrieve.
parameters.name: timesheetId

operations.description:
Create a new draft timesheet for the authenticated employee.

This endpoint creates a draft timesheet covering a specific work week (Monday to Sunday). The week start date provided by the employee determines both the start and end dates of the timesheet. All timelogs belonging to the employee that fall within the Monday through Sunday date range are automatically associated with the new draft timesheet.

The created timesheet remains in draft status until the employee submits it for approval. While in draft status, the employee can add or remove timelogs and modify the timesheet as needed. Each employee can have only one timesheet (draft, submitted, or approved) per week.

The response returns the complete created timesheet including the auto-calculated week end date, the initial total hours from included timelogs, and timestamps for creation.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Validate the authenticated employee exists and has an active status in the current organization context. Validate that week_start_date is a Monday. Calculate week_end_date as the following Sunday (week_start_date + 6 days). Verify no existing timesheet (any status) exists for this employee with the same week_start_date. Query all timelogs belonging to the employee where timelog date falls within [week_start_date, week_end_date]. Calculate total_hours by summing all found timelogs. Create the timesheet with status 'draft', include all found timelogs via the erp_hrm_timesheet_timelogs junction table. Return the created timesheet with associated timelogs and employee information.

responseBody.description: The created draft timesheet with auto-included timelogs

requestBody.description: Week start date (Monday) for the timesheet to be created

operations.description:
Update an existing timesheet owned by the authenticated employee.

This endpoint allows employees to modify their draft timesheets before submission or after rejection. Timesheets with status 'submitted' or 'approved' cannot be modified through this endpoint.

When a timesheet is rejected by a reviewer, it automatically returns to draft status, allowing the employee to make corrections and resubmit. The rejection reason provided by the reviewer is visible on the timesheet and should be addressed before resubmission.

Only the employee who owns the timesheet can update it. If the timesheet is rejected, updating it does not automatically resubmit - the employee must explicitly submit again after making corrections.

The week_start_date and week_end_date cannot be changed once the timesheet has been submitted, as these define the immutable billing period.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Retrieve the timesheet by timesheetId from erp_hrm_timesheets table.
2. Verify the authenticated employee owns this timesheet (erp_hrm_employee_id matches current user session employee).
3. If timesheet status is not 'draft', return 403 Forbidden with message indicating only draft timesheets can be updated.
4. Validate request body fields according to IErpHrmTimesheet.IUpdate schema.
5. Update only the provided fields: status transition to 'submitted', rejection_reason, week_start_date, week_end_date.
6. If status is changed to 'submitted', validate: timesheet contains at least one timelog, no duplicate submitted/approved timesheet exists for same employee and week.
7. If status is changed to 'submitted', set submitted_at to current timestamp.
8. Recalculate total_hours from associated timelogs in erp_hrm_timesheet_timelogs junction table.
9. Update updated_at timestamp.
10. Return the updated IErpHrmTimesheet entity.

responseBody.description: The updated timesheet entity with all current field values including updated status, timestamps, and total hours.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timesheet to update
parameters.name: timesheetId

requestBody.description: Fields to update on the timesheet. Only draft timesheets (including rejected timesheets) can be updated. Status can be changed to 'submitted' for submission workflow.

prerequisites.description: Timesheet must be created first via POST before it can be updated. The PUT operation updates an existing timesheet, so the timesheet record must exist (created via POST /erpHrm/member/timesheets) before attempting to update it.

operations.description:
Submit a draft timesheet for manager approval.

This operation transitions a timesheet from draft status to submitted status, entering the approval workflow. Only timesheets in draft status can be submitted. The system validates that the timesheet contains at least one timelog and that no other timesheet for the same employee and week already exists with submitted or approved status.

Upon successful submission, the timesheet is locked from further modifications by the employee until it has been reviewed. The submitting employee must be the owner of the timesheet. Managers with time:approve permission review submitted timesheets.

The response returns the updated timesheet with submitted_at timestamp recorded.
operations.name: submit
operations.specification:
Execute timesheet submission workflow for draft timesheets.

1. Validate the timesheet exists in erp_hrm_timesheets with the given timesheetId.
2. Verify the authenticated employee is the owner of the timesheet (erp_hrm_employee_id matches session employee).
3. Verify the timesheet status equals 'draft'. Reject if status is 'submitted', 'approved', or 'rejected'.
4. Query erp_hrm_timesheet_timelogs to verify the timesheet contains at least one timelog. Reject submission if no timelogs are associated.
5. Check for duplicate submission: query erp_hrm_timesheets to ensure no other timesheet exists for the same erp_hrm_employee_id and week_start_date with status 'submitted' or 'approved'. Reject if duplicate found.
6. Calculate total_hours by summing duration_minutes from all associated timelogs in erp_hrm_timesheet_timelogs joined with erp_hrm_timelogs.
7. Update the timesheet: set status to 'submitted', set submitted_at to current timestamp, update total_hours, update updated_at to current timestamp.
8. Return the updated timesheet with all fields including reviewer_employee relation (null) and timesheetTimelogs relation.

Edge cases:
- Timesheet not found: return 404
- Unauthorized (not owner): return 403
- Already submitted/approved/rejected: return 400 with appropriate message
- Empty timesheet (no timelogs): return 400 indicating timesheet must contain timelogs
- Duplicate week conflict: return 409 with message about existing submission

responseBody.description: The updated timesheet with submitted status and submission timestamp

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timesheet to submit (UUID format)
parameters.name: timesheetId

prerequisites.description: Create a draft timesheet that will be submitted for approval. The timesheet must exist with draft status before the submit operation can transition it to submitted status.

operations.description:
Permanently delete a draft or rejected timesheet and remove all its associations with timelogs.

This operation permanently removes the timesheet and its link records from the database. The timelogs themselves are preserved and remain accessible outside any timesheet context. Only timesheets in draft or rejected status can be deleted; submitted or approved timesheets cannot be removed.

The requesting user must be either the timesheet owner or possess the time:manage permission. The system validates ownership and permission before proceeding with deletion. Once deleted, the timesheet cannot be recovered and any rejection reason is lost.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Validate the timesheet exists and belongs to the current organization context. Verify the requesting user is either the timesheet owner (erp_hrm_employee_id matches authenticated employee) or has time:manage permission.

Check timesheet status: if status is 'submitted' or 'approved', reject the deletion request with error 'TIMESHEET_NOT_DRAFT'. Only status 'draft' or 'rejected' can be deleted.

Delete the timesheet record from erp_hrm_timesheets table. The Cascade onDelete for erp_hrm_timesheet_timelogs will automatically remove association records.

Timelogs linked to this timesheet remain unchanged in erp_hrm_timelogs table.

Return 204 No Content on success. Return 404 Not Found if timesheetId does not exist in organization. Return 403 Forbidden if user lacks permission or timesheet belongs to another employee without time:manage. Return 400 Bad Request if timesheet status is not draft or rejected.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timesheet to delete
parameters.name: timesheetId

prerequisites.description: Timesheet must be created first before it can be deleted. The created timesheet ID is used as the timesheetId parameter for the delete operation.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific timesheet by its ID for a given member.

This endpoint returns a single timesheet belonging to the specified member. The timesheet includes all associated metadata such as status, total hours, submission and review timestamps, and the reviewer information.

Access control: Employees can view their own timesheets. Users with time:approve or time:view_all permission can view any timesheet within their organization.

The returned timesheet contains the full details including:
- Week start and end dates defining the timesheet period
- Current workflow status (draft, submitted, approved, rejected)
- Total hours calculated from included timelogs
- Submission and review timestamps
- Rejection reason if the timesheet was rejected

If the timesheet does not exist or the requesting user lacks permission to view it, the system returns an access denied response.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query erp_hrm_timesheets table by id, joining with erp_hrm_employees to verify erp_hrm_user_id matches memberId.

Authorization rules:
1. If requesting user is the owner of the timesheet (their user record matches the employee.user), allow access.
2. If requesting user has time:approve or time:view_all permission in the organization, allow access.
3. Otherwise, deny access with 403 Forbidden.

If timesheet is not found, return 404 Not Found.

Join with erp_hrm_employees to verify the member relationship and include employee details in response.

Join with erp_hrm_timesheet_timelogs to include the associated timelogs in the response.

Return the complete timesheet entity including all included timelogs and reviewer information.

responseBody.description: The complete timesheet entity with associated timelogs and reviewer information

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the member (user) who owns the timesheet
parameters.name: memberId

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the timesheet to retrieve
parameters.name: timesheetId

operations.description:
Approve a submitted timesheet for an employee.

This endpoint transitions a timesheet from submitted status to approved status. Upon approval, all timelogs included in the timesheet become permanently locked and cannot be edited or deleted.

The system records the approval timestamp and the reviewer employee who performed the approval action. Only users with time:approve permission within the same organization as the timesheet owner can approve timesheets.

The timesheet must be in submitted status to be approved. If the timesheet has already been reviewed (approved or rejected), the system returns an error indicating an invalid state transition.
operations.name: approve
operations.specification:
Implement the timesheet approval workflow:

1. **Authorization Check**: Verify the current user has time:approve permission in the organization context.

2. **Timesheet Validation**: Retrieve the timesheet by timesheetId. Ensure the timesheet exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null).

3. **Status Validation**: Confirm the timesheet status is "submitted". If status is "draft", "approved", or "rejected", return an appropriate error indicating invalid state transition.

4. **Approval Processing**: Within a database transaction:
   - Update status to "approved"
   - Set reviewed_at to current timestamp
   - Set erp_hrm_reviewer_employee_id to the current user's employee ID in the organization

5. **Timelog Locking**: All timelogs linked to this timesheet via erp_hrm_timesheet_timelogs junction table should be marked as non-editable (implementation-specific locking mechanism).

6. **Response**: Return the updated timesheet entity with reviewer information populated.

7. **Error Handling**:
   - 404 if timesheet not found or deleted
   - 403 if user lacks time:approve permission
   - 409 Conflict if timesheet is not in submitted status
   - 400 for other validation failures

responseBody.description: The updated timesheet entity with approval information including reviewer and timestamp

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timesheet to approve
parameters.name: timesheetId

prerequisites.description: Create the timesheet entity that will be approved. The timesheet starts in draft status and must exist before it can be submitted for approval.
Submit the draft timesheet, transitioning it to submitted status. The approval endpoint requires timesheet status to be submitted; attempting to approve a draft returns 409 Conflict.

operations.description:
Reject a submitted timesheet and return it to draft status for employee revision.

This operation allows authorized users with time:approve permission to reject a submitted timesheet. A rejection requires providing a mandatory reason that explains why the timesheet was rejected. The employee can then view the rejection reason, make necessary corrections to their timelogs, and resubmit the timesheet for approval.

When a timesheet is rejected, all associated timelogs are unlocked, allowing the employee to edit or remove entries. The timesheet status transitions from submitted back to draft. The rejection reason is stored with the timesheet and visible to the employee.

Only timesheets in submitted status can be rejected. Attempting to reject a timesheet that is already approved, rejected, or in draft status returns an error.
operations.name: reject
operations.specification:
Reject a submitted timesheet by timesheetId.

1. Validate the timesheetId path parameter is a valid UUID format.

2. Query the erp_hrm_timesheets table to find the timesheet by timesheetId within the current organization context.

3. Verify the timesheet exists and belongs to the current organization.

4. Verify the timesheet status is 'submitted' - reject if timesheet is already approved, rejected, or in draft status.

5. Validate the request body contains a non-empty rejectionReason field - this field is mandatory.

6. Update the timesheet:
   - Set status to 'rejected'
   - Set rejection_reason to the provided reason string
   - Set reviewed_at to current timestamp
   - Set reviewed_by_id to the authenticated user's employee record ID

7. Unlock all timelogs associated with this timesheet via the erp_hrm_timesheet_timelogs junction table. The timelogs should become editable again by the owning employee.

8. Return the updated timesheet with all included timelogs in the response body.

responseBody.description: The rejected timesheet with updated status, rejection reason, and review information.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timesheet to reject (UUID format, scoped to current organization).
parameters.name: timesheetId

requestBody.description: Rejection reason explaining why the timesheet was rejected (required).

operations.description:
Add or remove timelogs from a timesheet for managing timesheet entries.

This operation allows employees to modify which timelogs are associated with their timesheet before submission. Employees can add timelogs that fall within the timesheet's week date range and remove unwanted associations. Timelogs can only be added to or removed from timesheets with draft or rejected status. Submitted or approved timesheets are locked and cannot be modified.

When adding timelogs, the system validates that each timelog belongs to the requesting employee and falls within the Monday through Sunday date range of the timesheet. When removing timelogs, the original timelog data is preserved in the system. The association is removed but the timelog record itself remains.

Users with time:manage permission can modify timelog associations on any timesheet regardless of ownership.
operations.name: manage
operations.specification:
Implement the following logic for managing timesheet-timelog associations:

1. Validate the timesheet exists and retrieve its current status, employee ownership, and week date range.
2. Verify the requesting user has permission to modify this timesheet's timelogs (either owns it or has time:manage permission).
3. Reject the request if the timesheet status is submitted or approved (timesheets in these states are locked).
4. Process addTimelogIds: for each timelog ID, validate that the timelog belongs to the timesheet owner, falls within the week_start_date to week_end_date range, is not already associated with this timesheet, and create the association record.
5. Process removeTimelogIds: for each timelog ID, validate that the timelog is currently associated with this timesheet and delete the association record.
6. Recalculate and update the total_hours field on the timesheet after modifications.
7. Return the updated timesheet with its current timelog associations and total hours.

responseBody.description: Updated timesheet with modified timelog associations and recalculated total hours.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timesheet to modify timelog associations for
parameters.name: timesheetId

requestBody.description: Arrays of timelog IDs to add or remove from the timesheet.

prerequisites.description: The timesheet must exist before managing its timelog associations. This operation creates a draft timesheet owned by the employee, which is required as the container for timelog associations.

Timelog entries must exist before they can be associated with or removed from a timesheet. This operation creates timelog entries that will be added to the timesheet via the association management endpoint.

operations.description:
Retrieve all timelogs associated with a specific timesheet.

This endpoint returns the collection of timelog entries that are linked to the specified timesheet through the timesheet-timelog junction. The response includes complete timelog details including date, duration, project association, task (if any), description, and billable status.

Access is determined by ownership: employees can view timelogs on their own timesheets, while users with time:view_all permission can view timelogs on any employee's timesheet in the organization. The timesheet must exist and belong to the user's organization context.

The timelogs are returned in their association order (added_at from the junction table) with the most recently added entries appearing last.
operations.name: invert
operations.specification:
Query the erp_hrm_timesheets table to verify the timesheet exists and belongs to the authenticated user's organization.

If the timesheet does not exist, return 404 Not Found.

Query the erp_hrm_timesheet_timelogs junction table joining with erp_hrm_timelogs to retrieve all timelogs linked to this timesheet. Join with erp_hrm_projects table to include project details, and optionally join with erp_hrm_tasks table for task information.

Authorization check: Allow access if (1) the timesheet's erp_hrm_employee_id matches the authenticated employee's id, OR (2) the authenticated user has time:view_all permission.

If neither condition is met, return 403 Forbidden.

Order results by the junction table's added_at field ascending (earliest added first).

Return the collection of timelogs with their full details including project and task associations.

responseBody.description: Collection of timelog entries linked to the specified timesheet with inverted parent information

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timesheet (global scope)
parameters.name: timesheetId

prerequisites.description: Timesheet must exist before its timelogs can be retrieved. The GET operation validates timesheet existence and returns 404 if not found.

operations.description:
Start a new live timer session for real-time time tracking.

This endpoint initiates a timer that tracks time in real-time against a selected project. The timer records the start timestamp immediately and continues running until the employee stops or discards it.

Business rules:
- An employee can have at most one active timer at any given time
- The selected project must be one the employee is assigned to as a project member
- The optional task must belong to the selected project
- Only employees with active status can start timers
- Deactivated employees cannot start new timers

When stopped, the timer creates a timelog entry with the calculated duration. When discarded, no record is created.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
1. Extract the authenticated employee from the request context (via session token)
2. Validate employee status is 'active' - reject if deactivated
3. Check if employee already has an active timer in erp_hrm_timers table
   - Query: SELECT id FROM erp_hrm_timers WHERE erp_hrm_employee_id = {employeeId}
   - If exists, return 409 Conflict error with message 'An active timer already exists'
4. Validate erp_hrm_project_id exists in request body
5. Verify employee is assigned to the project via erp_hrm_project_members
   - Query: SELECT 1 FROM erp_hrm_project_members WHERE erp_hrm_employee_id = {employeeId} AND erp_hrm_project_id = {projectId}
   - If not found, return 400 Bad Request error
6. If erp_hrm_task_id is provided:
   - Verify task exists and belongs to the selected project
   - Query: SELECT 1 FROM erp_hrm_tasks WHERE id = {taskId} AND erp_hrm_project_id = {projectId}
   - If not found, return 400 Bad Request error
7. Create timer record:
   - id: generate UUID
   - erp_hrm_employee_id: from authenticated context
   - erp_hrm_project_id: from request body
   - erp_hrm_task_id: from request body (nullable)
   - started_at: current timestamp (UTC)
   - description: from request body (nullable)
   - created_at: current timestamp (UTC)
   - updated_at: current timestamp (UTC)
8. Return the created timer with 201 Created status

responseBody.description: The created timer entity with all its details

requestBody.description: Timer creation payload with project and optional task selection

operations.description:
Retrieve the currently running timer for the authenticated employee.

This endpoint returns the active timer owned by the authenticated employee. Each employee can have at most one timer running at any given time.

The response includes the timer's complete details: the associated project and optional task, the description of work being tracked, the start timestamp, and the elapsed time calculated from the start timestamp to the current time.

If the authenticated employee has no running timer, the response returns null with a 200 status code.

This operation respects timer privacy — employees cannot view other employees' active timers. The existence of another employee's timer is never exposed through any API endpoint.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query the erp_hrm_timers table filtering by erp_hrm_employee_id matching the authenticated employee from session context. Enforce @@unique constraint ensures at most one timer per employee. Join with erp_hrm_projects to include project details (name, color) and with erp_hrm_tasks to include task details (title) when task_id is present. Calculate elapsed time as current_time minus started_at. Return null if no active timer found. If timer exists, return complete timer details including nested project and task objects. Handle deactivated employee by rejecting request with appropriate error.

responseBody.description: The authenticated employee's active timer with associated project and task details, or null if no timer is running.

operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated employee's timer records with optional filtering.

This endpoint allows employees to view their running timer status and search through their timer history. Each employee can have at most one active timer at a time, enforced by the database unique constraint on employee_id.

Timer records are private to the employee who created them. Other employees, including managers and project leads, cannot view another employee's timers. Only the employee who owns the timer and organization administrators with system-level access can retrieve timer information.

The response includes the timer details along with associated project and task information. If no active timer exists, an empty result is returned.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the erp_hrm_timers table filtering by the authenticated employee's ID from the session context.

Apply optional filters from the request body:
- Filter by erp_hrm_project_id if project filter is provided
- Filter by timer status if specified (active/running only)

Join with erp_hrm_projects table to include project details (name, color_code) in the response.
Join with erp_hrm_tasks table to include task details (title) if a task is associated.

Return timer records sorted by started_at descending (most recent first).
Apply pagination with configurable page size.

If no timer exists for the employee, return empty array.

Ensure data isolation: only return timers belonging to the authenticated employee.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of timer records belonging to the authenticated employee

requestBody.description: Optional search filters for timer queries including project filter

operations.description:
Update the currently running timer for the authenticated employee.

This operation allows employees to modify the properties of their active timer while it is running. The update can change the description, selected project, and/or task being tracked. The original start timestamp is preserved regardless of any edits made.

The project can be changed to any project the employee is assigned to as a project member. When changing the project, any previously selected task is cleared if it does not belong to the new project. Task can only be changed to tasks within the currently selected project.

This endpoint only operates on the employee's own active timer. Other employees' timers are not accessible through this operation.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update the running timer associated with the authenticated employee.

Implementation steps:
1. Extract employee_id from authenticated session context
2. Query erp_hrm_timers table to find the active timer for this employee (using the unique constraint on erp_hrm_employee_id)
3. If no active timer exists, return error indicating no running timer to update
4. Validate the request body:
   - If project_id is provided, verify employee is assigned to that project (check erp_hrm_project_members)
   - If task_id is provided, verify task belongs to the selected project (check erp_hrm_tasks)
5. Update only the fields provided in the request body:
   - description: optional string
   - project_id: optional UUID, must be assigned project membership
   - task_id: optional UUID, must belong to selected project
6. When updating project_id, clear task_id if the previous task does not belong to new project
7. Update updated_at timestamp
8. Return the complete updated timer entity with all fields including the original started_at

Edge cases:
- Employee has no active timer: return 404 with message
- Project not assigned to employee: return 400 with validation error
- Task does not belong to project: return 400 with validation error
- Deactivated employee: return 403 error
- Only include fields that are explicitly provided in request

responseBody.description: The updated timer entity with all current properties including original start timestamp

requestBody.description: Fields to update on the running timer - all fields are optional

prerequisites.description: A running timer must already exist before it can be updated. The authenticated employee must start a timer first via POST /erpHrm/member/timers to create the active timer record that will be modified.

operations.description:
Discard the employee's currently active timer.

This operation immediately terminates the specified timer without creating a timelog entry. The timer must belong to the authenticated employee making the request. Once discarded, the timer is permanently removed and cannot be recovered.

The employee must have an active timer to discard. If the timer does not exist or belongs to another employee, the system returns a not found error. This operation does not generate any activity log entry since discarded timers do not create historical records.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification: Validate that the timer exists in the database. Verify the timer belongs to the authenticated employee by matching erp_hrm_employee_id with the current session's employee record. If the timer does not exist, return 404 not found error. If the timer belongs to another employee, return 404 not found error (do not reveal existence of other employees' timers for privacy). Permanently delete the timer record from erp_hrm_timers table using cascade delete. Do not create any timelog entry. Do not create any activity log entry. Return 204 No Content on success.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the timer to discard
parameters.name: timerId

prerequisites.description: The timer must be created (started) before it can be discarded. The POST /erpHrm/member/timers operation creates a new timer session that can subsequently be deleted via the discard operation.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of invitations sent by an organization.

This operation returns all invitations associated with the specified organization. Users can filter the results by invitation status (pending, accepted, expired), search by email address, and sort the results. The response includes invitation details such as the invited email, current status, timestamps, and any pre-assigned role or department.

This endpoint requires the `employee:manage` permission within the organization context. Only invitations belonging to the specified organization are accessible. The list is paginated to handle large result sets efficiently.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query erp_hrm_invitations table filtered by erp_hrm_organization_id from path parameter.

Apply search filters:
- Filter by status if provided (pending, accepted, expired values)
- Search by email using partial match (ILIKE for case-insensitive matching)
- Filter by date range on created_at if provided

Join with erp_hrm_roles table to include role name in response when role_id is set.
Join with erp_hrm_departments table to include department name in response when department_id is set.

Exclude soft-deleted records where deleted_at is not null.

Apply cursor-based or offset pagination with configurable page size.

Sort by created_at descending by default (most recent first).

Return paginated response with total count, page metadata, and invitation summaries.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of invitation summaries filtered by the provided criteria

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the organization (global scope)
parameters.name: organizationId

requestBody.description: Search criteria, filters, and pagination parameters for invitation list

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific invitation by its unique identifier within an organization.

This endpoint returns the complete invitation details including the invited email address, current status (pending, accepted, or expired), the pre-assigned role and department if specified, the inviter's note, and relevant timestamps for creation and expiration.

The invitation must belong to the specified organization. Users can only retrieve invitations from organizations they are members of. The response includes related role and department information when they were pre-assigned during invitation creation.

This operation is typically used when displaying invitation details before deciding to resend or cancel, or when navigating from an invitation list to its full details.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query erp_hrm_invitations table by id, ensuring the invitation belongs to the specified organization.

Validate that:
1. The invitation with given id exists
2. The invitation's erp_hrm_organization_id matches the path parameter organizationId
3. The invitation has not been soft-deleted (deleted_at is null)

Join with erp_hrm_roles table to include role name and code in the response.
Join with erp_hrm_departments table to include department name in the response.

If invitation not found or does not belong to the organization, return 404 error.

Return the full invitation entity including all fields: id, email, status, token (for pending invitations), position, note, role details, department details, accepted_at, expires_at, created_at, updated_at.

responseBody.description: The invitation entity with related role and department information

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the organization (UUID, global scope)
parameters.name: organizationId

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the invitation (UUID)
parameters.name: invitationId

operations.description:
Create and send a new invitation to a prospective employee to join the organization.

This operation allows organization managers to invite users by email address. The invitation process handles two scenarios:

1. **Existing user**: If the email matches an existing user account, the user is immediately added to the organization as an active employee with the assigned role, department, and position. The invitation status is marked as accepted.

2. **New user**: If the email does not match any existing account, a pending invitation is created. When the user eventually registers with that email, they are automatically associated with the organization.

The system prevents duplicate pending invitations for the same email address within an organization. Only users with `employee:manage` permission can create invitations. All invitations are scoped to the organization specified in the path parameter.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
1. Extract organizationId from path parameter (must be valid UUID)
2. Extract email and optional fields from request body: roleId, departmentId, position, note
3. Validate email format using RFC 5322 email validation rules
4. Validate that optional roleId exists in the organization if provided
5. Validate that optional departmentId exists in the organization if provided
6. Query erp_hrm_invitations table to check for existing pending invitation with same erp_hrm_organization_id + email combination
7. If duplicate pending invitation exists, return 409 Conflict error
8. Generate unique invitation token (secure random string, min 32 characters)
9. Set expiration date (default: 30 days from creation)
10. Insert new invitation record into erp_hrm_invitations table with status 'pending'
11. Check if user exists with matching email in erp_hrm_members table
12. If user exists:
    a. Query default role for the organization
    b. Create employee record linking user to organization with assigned role/department/position
    c. Update invitation status to 'accepted' and set accepted_at timestamp
    d. Return invitation with accepted status
13. If user does not exist:
    a. Return invitation with pending status
14. Log activity in activity log (invitation sent)

Edge cases:
- Invalid email format: return 400 Bad Request
- Role not found or not in organization: return 400 Bad Request
- Department not found or not in organization: return 400 Bad Request
- Duplicate pending invitation: return 409 Conflict
- Organization not found: return 404 Not Found

responseBody.description: The created invitation entity with its current status. If the invited email belongs to an existing user, the invitation status will be 'accepted' and the employee was created immediately.

operations.description:
Update an existing invitation within an organization.

This endpoint allows users with employee:manage permission to modify invitation details before the invitation is accepted or expired. The operation updates the invitation record with new role assignments, department, position, or corrected email address.

Only pending invitations can be updated. Accepted invitations should be managed through employee deactivation, and expired invitations cannot be modified.

The invitation is scoped to the organization specified in the path, ensuring proper data isolation between organizations.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Implement the invitation update operation:

1. **Authorization Check**: Verify the requesting user has employee:manage permission in the organization specified by organizationId

2. **Input Validation**:
   - Validate organizationId matches the user's current organization context
   - Validate invitationId is a valid UUID format
   - Validate that the invitation exists and belongs to the specified organization
   - Validate that the invitation status is 'pending' (only pending invitations can be updated)
   - Validate email format if provided
   - Validate role_id references an existing role in the organization if provided
   - Validate department_id references an existing department in the organization if provided

3. **Business Rules**:
   - Prevent updating accepted or expired invitations
   - If email is changed, check for duplicate pending invitation with same email and organization
   - Update the updated_at timestamp

4. **Database Operation**:
   - Update only the provided fields in erp_hrm_invitations table
   - Use optimistic locking with updated_at for concurrent updates

5. **Response**: Return the complete updated invitation record including:
   - id, email, status, token, position, note
   - role and department assignments (if any)
   - timestamps (created_at, updated_at, accepted_at, expires_at)

6. **Error Handling**:
   - 403 Forbidden: User lacks employee:manage permission
   - 404 Not Found: Invitation does not exist or belongs to different organization
   - 400 Bad Request: Invalid input data or trying to update non-pending invitation

responseBody.description: The updated invitation record with all fields including role and department assignments

operations.description:
Cancel a pending invitation in the organization.

This operation cancels a pending invitation by marking it as deleted. Only invitations with status 'pending' can be cancelled through this operation. Accepted or expired invitations cannot be cancelled; instead, the associated employee record must be deactivated through employee management.

Once cancelled, the invitation is immediately invalidated and cannot be reinstated. The invited user will no longer be automatically added to the organization if they register with the invited email address after cancellation.

This operation performs a soft delete on the invitation record, preserving the data for audit purposes while preventing future processing. It requires the employee:manage permission and operates within the currently selected organization context.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification: Validate that the invitation exists and belongs to the specified organization. Verify the invitation status is 'pending' - reject with 400 error if invitation is already accepted or expired. Perform soft delete by setting the deleted_at timestamp to current time. Return 204 No Content on successful deletion. Log the cancellation in the activity log with action type 'invitation_cancelled'.

operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated user's dashboard with personalized metrics and organizational overview.

This endpoint returns dashboard data scoped to the user's current organization. All authenticated employees receive personal metrics including hours logged today and this week, active timer status, recent time entries, pending timesheet for the current week, and tasks assigned to them with open or in-progress status.

Users with the report:view permission additionally receive organizational metrics showing total active employees in the organization, total hours logged by all employees this week, count of timesheets awaiting approval, projects with budget utilization exceeding 80%, and the top 5 employees by hours logged this week.

The dashboard data refreshes automatically as time entries are logged and timesheets are submitted or reviewed. The response structure adapts based on the requesting user's role and permissions within the organization.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the database to build dashboard metrics for the authenticated user's organization.

1. Load session context to get: current organization ID, current employee ID, user's role permissions
2. Build personal metrics (always included):
   - Query erp_hrm_timelogs for today's hours: filter by erp_hrm_employee_id and date = today
   - Query erp_hrm_timelogs for this week's hours: filter by erp_hrm_employee_id and week containing current date
   - Query erp_hrm_timers for active timer: filter by erp_hrm_employee_id with no associated timelog (timer not stopped)
   - Query erp_hrm_timelogs for recent entries: last 5 timelogs ordered by created_at DESC
   - Query erp_hrm_timesheets for pending timesheet: find draft or submitted timesheet for current week (week_start_date = current Monday)
   - Query erp_hrm_tasks for assigned tasks: filter by erp_hrm_employee_id and status IN ('open', 'in-progress')
3. If user has report:view permission, build organizational metrics:
   - Count erp_hrm_employees where status = 'active' for the organization
   - Sum erp_hrm_timelogs hours for current week (all employees)
   - Count erp_hrm_timesheets where status = 'submitted'
   - Query erp_hrm_projects joining erp_hrm_timelogs to find budget utilization > 80% (exclude projects with null budget_hours)
   - Query top 5 employees by total hours logged this week, join employee names
4. Return aggregated dashboard response with personal section always present, organizational section only if report:view permission exists

responseBody.description: Dashboard response containing personal metrics for all authenticated users and organizational metrics for users with report:view permission.

operations.description:
Set the active organization context for the current session.

This endpoint allows users who belong to multiple organizations to switch between them. When a user selects an organization, all subsequent API operations are scoped to that organization until the context is changed again.

The user must be a member of the target organization to successfully switch context. Only organizations where the user has an active employee record are available for selection.

This operation updates the session state to reflect the newly selected organization. The response includes organization details and the user's permissions within that organization context.
operations.name: select
operations.specification:
Validate the user making the request is authenticated.
Extract the user ID from the current session.
Verify the user has an active employee record in the target organization.
Retrieve the employee record for the user within the target organization, including their role.
Retrieve all permissions assigned to the employee's role.
Update the session to set the new organization context.
Return the organization details, employee information, and role permissions.

Edge cases:
- If the user is not a member of the target organization, return 403 Forbidden.
- If the employee record is deactivated, return 403 Forbidden.
- If the target organization does not exist, return 404 Not Found.
- If no organization is specified in the request, return 400 Bad Request.

responseBody.description: The new organization context including organization details, employee information, and role permissions

requestBody.description: The organization identifier to switch to

operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated statistics for the current organization dashboard.

This endpoint provides real-time organizational metrics including the total count of active employees, total hours logged this week across all employees, the number of timesheets awaiting approval, and a list of projects where budget utilization has exceeded 80 percent.

Additionally, the response includes the top five employees ranked by hours logged during the current week, showing each employee's name, department, and total hours. This endpoint requires the report:view permission and all statistics are scoped to the currently selected organization context.
operations.name: overview
operations.specification:
Query the current organization context from the session. Verify the requesting user has report:view permission in their role.

Calculate active employee count from erp_hrm_employees where organization_id matches and status equals active.

Calculate total hours logged this week from erp_hrm_timelogs where log_date falls within Monday to Sunday of current week and employee belongs to current organization.

Count pending timesheets from erp_hrm_timesheets where status equals submitted and employee belongs to current organization.

Query projects with budget_hours > 0 from erp_hrm_projects where (actual_hours / budget_hours) * 100 >= 80, sorted by utilization percentage descending, limit to 10.

Find top 5 employees this week from timelogs aggregation, join with erp_hrm_employees for name and department, sort by total hours descending.

Return all statistics in a single response object with clear category groupings.

responseBody.description: Organization statistics including employee count, weekly hours, pending timesheets, high-utilization projects, and top performers.

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete department hierarchy for the current organization as a tree structure.

This endpoint returns all departments organized by their parent-child relationships, enabling hierarchical displays in UI components such as tree views and organizational charts. Each department node includes its direct children, allowing recursive rendering.

The hierarchy respects the one-level nesting constraint: departments may have a parent, but that parent cannot have its own parent. Root-level departments (those without parents) appear at the top level of the response, with their child departments nested within.

Departments are scoped to the currently selected organization, ensuring data isolation between organizations. Both active and inactive departments are included in the hierarchy.
operations.name: hierarchy
operations.specification:
Query the erp_hrm_departments table filtering by the current organization context.

Build the hierarchy tree structure server-side:
1. Fetch all departments belonging to the organization where deleted_at IS NULL or deleted_at IS NOT NULL (include both active and inactive)
2. Group departments by their parent_id
3. Identify root-level departments (where parent_id is null)
4. For each root department, recursively nest its children (one level deep only, since schema enforces this)
5. Sort departments alphabetically by name within each level

Return the tree structure with each node containing:
- Full department details (id, name, description)
- Parent reference for context
- Children array (may be empty)

Handle edge cases:
- Empty organization: return empty children array
- Departments with deleted parents: include them as root-level in hierarchy

responseBody.description: Hierarchical tree structure of departments with nested children

operations.description:
Retrieve the complete list of available permissions that can be assigned to roles within an organization.

This endpoint returns all predefined permission codes that define what actions users can perform. Permissions include organization management, employee management, project operations, time tracking controls, and report access. Organization owners and users with appropriate permissions can view this list to understand available capabilities when creating or editing custom roles.

The response includes permission codes along with basic metadata such as creation timestamps. This endpoint does not filter by organization since permissions are system-wide definitions.
operations.name: list
operations.specification:
Query the erp_hrm_role_permissions table to retrieve all distinct permission codes available in the system.

1. Execute a SELECT DISTINCT query on the permission column from erp_hrm_role_permissions to get all unique permission codes.

2. Join with erp_hrm_roles to include role context (role ID, role name) for each permission.

3. Order results alphabetically by permission code for consistent output.

4. Return the permission codes along with associated role information (role_id, role_name).

5. No pagination required as the set of permissions is fixed and small.

6. No organization filtering needed since permissions are system-wide definitions.

responseBody.description: An array of available permissions with their associated role information.

operations.description:
Replace all permissions assigned to a role with a new set of permissions.

This bulk update operation replaces the entire permission set of a custom role. The request body should contain the complete list of permission codes to assign. Permissions not included in the request are removed from the role.

Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) cannot be modified. Attempting to update permissions for a built-in role returns a validation error. Only organization owners with org:manage permission can modify custom roles.

The operation validates that all provided permission codes are valid system permissions. Duplicate permissions in the request are deduplicated before storage.
operations.name: bulkUpdate
operations.specification:
1. Validate roleId exists and belongs to the current organization context
2. Retrieve the role from erp_hrm_roles table
3. Check role.is_builtin flag - if true, reject with 400 error
4. Validate all permission codes in request body against allowed permissions list: org:manage, employee:manage, employee:view, project:manage, project:view, time:manage, time:approve, time:view_all, report:view
5. Begin transaction:
   a. Delete all existing entries from erp_hrm_role_permissions where erp_hrm_role_id matches
   b. Insert new permission entries for each permission in request body
   c. Update role.updated_at timestamp
6. Commit transaction
7. Return the updated role with its new permission set

Edge cases:
- Empty permissions array: clears all permissions (valid scenario for minimal access roles)
- Invalid permission code: reject with 400 error listing invalid codes
- Non-existent role: return 404 error
- Role from different organization: return 404 (not 403 to prevent enumeration)

responseBody.description: The role entity with its updated permission set

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the role (UUID format)
parameters.name: roleId

requestBody.description: Array of permission codes to assign to the role

prerequisites.description: Role must exist before its permissions can be updated. The bulk update operation references a role via roleId path parameter, which must be a valid role created first.

operations.description:
Validate whether a role name is available for use in the current organization.

This endpoint checks if a proposed role name meets all naming constraints before attempting creation. It validates that the name is unique within the organization and does not conflict with built-in role names. Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) are protected and cannot be duplicated.

The validation checks include: name uniqueness within the organization scope, prevention of built-in role name conflicts, and proper character constraints. This operation is typically called before creating a custom role to provide immediate feedback to users.

Errors returned indicate specific validation failures, allowing users to correct their input without attempting an invalid creation.
operations.name: validate
operations.specification:
Query erp_hrm_roles table to check if a role with the given name already exists in the current organization context.

Validate role name against the following rules:
1. Check if role name matches any built-in role name (case-insensitive): 'owner', 'manager', 'employee'
2. Check if role name already exists in the current organization (case-insensitive uniqueness)
3. Return all validation errors found

The validation should be case-insensitive when comparing names. Return a result object with isValid boolean and an array of error messages for any validation failures.

responseBody.description: Validation result indicating whether the role name is valid and any error messages if invalid

requestBody.description: Role name to validate for availability in the current organization

operations.description:
Retrieve a budget utilization report comparing estimated budget hours against actual hours logged for all projects in the organization.

This endpoint calculates budget consumption metrics for each project that has budget hours configured. For each project, it displays the budget hours value, the sum of all timelog durations logged against the project, the percentage of budget consumed, and the budget status indicator.

Projects without budget hours are automatically excluded from the report as they have no baseline for comparison. The response is sorted by budget utilization percentage in descending order to highlight projects approaching or exceeding their budgets first.

This operation requires the report:view permission and returns data scoped to the user's current organization context.
operations.name: budgetReport
operations.specification:
Query all projects belonging to the authenticated user's organization from erp_hrm_projects table.

Filter the projects to include only those where budget_hours is NOT NULL AND budget_hours > 0.

For each included project, calculate actual_hours_logged by:
1. Query erp_hrm_timelogs table for all timelogs where erp_hrm_project_id matches the project id
2. Sum the duration_minutes values
3. Convert from minutes to hours by dividing by 60
4. Round to one decimal place

Calculate budget_utilization_percentage for each project:
1. Formula: (actual_hours_logged / budget_hours) * 100
2. Round to one decimal place
3. Values can exceed 100 when actual hours exceed budget hours

Determine budget_status for each project:
1. If actual_hours_logged > budget_hours: status = 'over_budget'
2. Else if budget_utilization_percentage >= 80: status = 'approaching_budget'
3. Else: status = 'within_budget'

Sort results by budget_utilization_percentage in descending order (highest utilization first).

Return the calculated values for each project including: project id, project name, budget_hours, actual_hours_logged, budget_utilization_percentage, and budget_status.

If no projects have budget hours configured, return an empty projects array.

responseBody.description: Budget utilization report containing an array of project budget comparisons with calculated metrics.

operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated analytics and statistics about members assigned to a specific project.

This endpoint returns project member analytics including total member count, breakdown by assigned role (member vs project_lead), and a list of current project members with their role assignments and join dates. The analytics are scoped to the specified project within the user's current organization context.

The response includes summary statistics for quick overview and detailed member list for further analysis. Project membership authorization applies - users must have project view permissions to access this endpoint.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query erp_hrm_projects table to validate projectId exists and belongs to the user's organization.
Join erp_hrm_project_members with erp_hrm_employees to get member details.
Aggregate member count by assigned_role (member, project_lead).
Calculate total member count.
Return summary statistics and member details ordered by created_at.

Validate that the project belongs to the user's current organization context.
Return empty analytics (not error) if project has no members.

Error handling:
- 404 if projectId does not exist or belongs to different organization
- 403 if user lacks project view permission

responseBody.description: Project member analytics including summary statistics and member list

operations.description:
Retrieve comprehensive analytics and statistics about tasks within a specific project.

This endpoint provides aggregated metrics that help project leads and managers understand task distribution, progress, and workload within the project. The analytics include status breakdowns showing how many tasks are open, in-progress, completed, and closed, as well as priority distribution across low, medium, high, and urgent levels.

The response includes completion metrics calculated from total versus completed tasks, average estimated hours for tasks with estimates, and overdue task counts based on due date comparison with current timestamp. Temporal trends show task creation patterns over the last 30 days.

This operation requires the requesting user to have project:view or project:manage permission for the specified project. Users can only access analytics for projects they are members of or have organization-level project management permissions.
operations.name: analytics
operations.specification:
Query erp_hrm_projects table to verify project exists and user has access permission. Return 404 if project not found.

Query erp_hrm_tasks table filtered by erp_hrm_project_id matching the path parameter.

Execute the following aggregations:
1. Status breakdown: COUNT tasks grouped by status field (open, in-progress, completed, closed)
2. Priority breakdown: COUNT tasks grouped by priority field (low, medium, high, urgent)
3. Completion rate: total_tasks > 0 ? (completed_tasks + closed_tasks) / total_tasks * 100 : 0
4. Average estimated hours: AVG(estimated_hours) WHERE estimated_hours IS NOT NULL
5. Overdue tasks: COUNT WHERE due_date < CURRENT_TIMESTAMP AND status NOT IN ('completed', 'closed')
6. Temporal trend: COUNT tasks created in last 30 days, grouped by date

Join with erp_hrm_employees table for assignee information if needed for detailed breakdowns.

Apply organization context filtering via erp_hrm_projects.erp_hrm_organization_id matching the authenticated user's organization scope.

Return computed analytics object with all aggregated metrics. Handle empty project (no tasks) by returning zero counts for all metrics.

responseBody.description: Analytics object containing task statistics for the specified project including status distribution, priority breakdown, completion metrics, and overdue task count.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the project to retrieve task analytics for (UUID format)
parameters.name: projectId

operations.description:
Stop the authenticated employee's active timer and optionally create a timelog entry.

When an employee requests to stop their running timer, the system calculates the duration from the start timestamp to the current time, rounds it to the nearest minute, and creates a corresponding timelog entry. The timer is then removed from the system.

If the discard option is specified, the timer is stopped without creating any timelog entry. This allows employees to abandon time tracking without generating records.

The resulting timelog includes the project, optional task, calculated duration, and description from the timer. The billable flag is set to true by default. The timelog date is set to the current date.

Only employees with active status can stop timers. Deactivated employees cannot perform this operation.
operations.name: stop
operations.specification:
Stop timer operation flow:

1. Retrieve authenticated employee from session context
2. Query erp_hrm_timers table for timer with erp_hrm_employee_id matching authenticated employee
3. Verify timer exists - return 404 if no active timer found
4. Verify employee status is active - return 403 if deactivated
5. Calculate duration: current_time - timer.started_at in minutes
6. Round duration: if seconds < 30, round down to 0; if seconds >= 30, round up to next minute
7. If request body discard flag is true:
   - Delete timer from erp_hrm_timers table
   - Return empty response with 204 status
8. If discard flag is false (default):
   - Create new erp_hrm_timelogs entry with:
     * erp_hrm_employee_id: from timer
     * erp_hrm_project_id: from timer
     * erp_hrm_task_id: from timer (nullable)
     * date: current date at midnight (date-only, ignore time)
     * duration_minutes: calculated rounded duration
     * description: from timer description
     * billable: true (default)
   - Delete timer from erp_hrm_timers table
   - Return created timelog with 201 status

Edge cases:
- Timer with no description: proceed with null description
- Timer with no task: proceed with null erp_hrm_task_id
- Concurrent stop requests: use database transaction to ensure atomicity
- Very long running timer: no time limit, calculate as-is

responseBody.description: The created timelog entry from stopped timer. Contains project, task, date, duration, description, and billable flag.

requestBody.description: Optional flag to discard timer without creating timelog. Defaults to false.

operations.description:
Retrieve the organization dashboard with aggregate metrics for the current organization.

This endpoint provides a comprehensive overview of the organization's current state, including employee count, weekly time tracking summaries, pending approval items, and budget utilization alerts. The dashboard is scoped to the currently selected organization context.

The response includes total active employee count, total hours logged across all employees for the current week, the count of timesheets awaiting approval, a list of projects where budget utilization exceeds 80 percent, and the top performers by logged hours for the week.

Requires report:view or org:manage permission to access.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the currently selected organization context from the session. Verify the requesting user has report:view or org:manage permission.

1. Count active employees: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM erp_hrm_employees WHERE erp_hrm_organization_id = :orgId AND status = 'active'

2. Calculate total hours this week: Join erp_hrm_timelogs with erp_hrm_employees, filter by current week (Monday to Sunday based on org timezone), sum duration_minutes and convert to hours.

3. Count pending timesheets: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM erp_hrm_timesheets WHERE erp_hrm_employee_id IN (employee IDs for org) AND status = 'submitted'

4. Find projects with budget over 80%: Join erp_hrm_projects with timelog aggregates, calculate (actual_hours / budget_hours * 100), filter where percentage > 80 AND budget_hours IS NOT NULL AND status = 'active'.

5. Get top 5 employees by hours: Aggregate timelogs per employee for current week, order by total hours DESC, limit 5. Include employee name and total hours.

Return all metrics in a single response object. If no data exists for a category, return empty array or zero as appropriate.

responseBody.description: Organization dashboard with aggregate metrics including employee count, weekly hours, pending approvals, budget alerts, and top performers.

operations.description:
Generate a time analytics report with aggregated hours data.

This endpoint provides comprehensive time tracking analytics for the organization. Users with report:view permission can generate reports showing total hours logged within a specified date range, with flexible grouping and filtering options.

The report displays aggregated time data grouped by the selected dimension (employee, project, or task). Each grouping includes total hours, billable hours subtotal, and non-billable hours subtotal. When grouping by employee, the report also includes employee details such as department and position.

Filtering capabilities allow narrowing results to specific employees, projects, or billable status. The response includes both detailed breakdowns and summary totals for quick overview.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the erp_hrm_timelogs table with the provided date range filter.

Join erp_hrm_timelogs with erp_hrm_employees to get employee details (name, department, position). Join with erp_hrm_projects to get project details (name, color). Join with erp_hrm_tasks optionally for task-based grouping.

Apply date range filter: timelogs where date >= start_date AND date <= end_date.

Apply optional filters:
- employee_id: filter by specific employee
- project_id: filter by specific project
- task_id: filter by specific task
- billable: true = billable only, false = non-billable only, null = all

Group results by the specified group_by field:
- 'employee': group by erp_hrm_employee_id, include employee details
- 'project': group by erp_hrm_project_id, include project details
- 'task': group by erp_hrm_task_id, include task details

For each group, calculate:
- total_minutes: SUM(duration_minutes)
- billable_minutes: SUM(duration_minutes) WHERE billable = true
- non_billable_minutes: SUM(duration_minutes) WHERE billable = false
- timelog_count: COUNT(*)

Sort by total_hours descending within each group.

Return paginated results with pagination parameters.

operations.description:
Generate a time analytics report with aggregated hours data.

This endpoint provides comprehensive time tracking analytics for the organization. Users with report:view permission can generate reports showing total hours logged within a specified date range, with flexible grouping and filtering options.

The report displays aggregated time data grouped by the selected dimension (employee, project, or task). Each grouping includes total hours, billable hours subtotal, and non-billable hours subtotal. When grouping by employee, the report also includes employee details such as department and position.

Filtering capabilities allow narrowing results to specific employees, projects, or billable status. The response includes both detailed breakdowns and summary totals for quick overview.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the erp_hrm_timelogs table with the provided date range filter.

Join erp_hrm_timelogs with erp_hrm_employees to get employee details (name, department, position). Join with erp_hrm_projects to get project details (name, color). Join with erp_hrm_tasks optionally for task-based grouping.

Apply date range filter: timelogs where date >= start_date AND date <= end_date.

Apply optional filters:
- employee_id: filter by specific employee
- project_id: filter by specific project
- task_id: filter by specific task
- billable: true = billable only, false = non-billable only, null = all

Group results by the specified group_by field:
- 'employee': group by erp_hrm_employee_id, include employee details
- 'project': group by erp_hrm_project_id, include project details
- 'task': group by erp_hrm_task_id, include task details

For each group, calculate:
- total_minutes: SUM(duration_minutes)
- billable_minutes: SUM(duration_minutes) WHERE billable = true
- non_billable_minutes: SUM(duration_minutes) WHERE billable = false
- timelog_count: COUNT(*)

Sort by total_hours descending within each group.

Return paginated results with pagination parameters.
